task.title: Prepare declarative workflow definitions as inert topology
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/677 under decision https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/676 by converting selected workflow YAML into bounded, descriptor-revalidated, immutable state-machine definitions without granting execution authority.
acceptance_criteria: Parse strict workflow_version 1 YAML and preserve exact workflow, phase, transition, target, and optional gate identifiers in authored order.
Reject wrong kinds before filesystem access and revalidate package, manifest, entrypoint, and descriptor identity through the shared descriptor-anchored boundary.
Reject invalid encoding, size, starts, phase identities, topology, targets, gates, and reachability deterministically and all-or-nothing.
Keep prepared definitions inert with no registration, execution, scheduling, persistence, gate resolution, action binding, provider call, or permission grant.

attempts.summary: Established RED integration coverage for bounded workflow preparation and complete graph validation.
attempts.diagnostic: The focused workflow_preparation test failed to compile because prepared workflow topology types and the preparation API did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added coverage for exact authored order, reachable cycles with terminal exits, wrong-kind preflight, strict encoding and YAML, version and unknown-field rejection, every graph invariant, exact size bounds, descriptor changes, empty selection, and all-or-nothing failure.

attempts.summary: Implemented descriptor-anchored parsing into immutable inert definitions.
attempts.diagnostic: Separating bounded artifact loading from strict parsing and complete topology validation reused the existing filesystem trust boundary while keeping workflow semantics explicit.
attempts.patch: Added prepared workflow, phase, and transition types; strict version-one YAML parsing; deterministic graph validation; typed sourced errors; ADR-0006; and extension documentation.

attempts.summary: Held the verified head when automated review reported a false green.
attempts.diagnostic: CodeRabbit reported review rate limiting despite a successful-looking status, so that status was not accepted as substantive exact-head review evidence and auto-merge remained disabled.
attempts.patch: Preserved head 70d4935d7babb54e1972d0b0802b8bec803ff287 until the cooldown and shared-budget check permitted one deliberate review resume; substantive review then covered all changed files with no actionable finding.

outcome.summary: Selected workflow YAML now becomes exact, bounded, statically validated inert topology suitable for later explicit admission while malformed graphs fail closed.

lessons: Complete graph validation belongs at the preparation boundary so malformed topology never becomes admitted workflow state.
Authored transition order and exact gate identifiers can be preserved as data without choosing an edge or evaluating a gate.
Descriptor-anchored revalidation and bounded reads are reusable filesystem trust primitives independent of artifact kind.
A successful-looking rate-limited review status is not substantive evidence; the exact head must remain unmerged through cooldown and deliberate resume.
Preparation validates inert data and grants no provider, tool, action, scheduling, persistence, or permission authority.
